title: Sample Paper: Calibration of Language Model Uncertainty via Temperature-Scaled Retrieval
abstract: We propose a retrieval-augmented temperature scaling method to recalibrate language model confidences on factoid QA, reducing expected calibration error from 12% to 3.4% without retraining.

sections.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Modern language models are systematically overconfident on rare entities.
Existing temperature scaling is global; we propose per-question scaling driven by retrieval evidence count.

sections.heading: Method
paragraphs: Given a question, we retrieve k passages and set the temperature as T = T0 * f(retrieval_score).
f is a learned monotone function fit on a held-out validation set.

sections.heading: Experiments
paragraphs: On Natural Questions, we report ECE of 3.4% (vs. 12% baseline) and Brier score of 0.18.
We ablate the f function: piecewise-linear vs. sigmoid; piecewise-linear wins by 0.6 ECE points.

citations.raw: Guo et al., On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks, 2017.
